question: A 43-year-old male is transferred from an outside hospital to the neurologic intensive care unit for management of a traumatic brain injury after suffering a 30-foot fall from a roof-top. He now lacks decision-making capacity but does not fulfill the criteria for brain-death. The patient does not have a living will and did not name a specific surrogate decision-maker or durable power of attorney. Which of the following would be the most appropriate person to name as a surrogate decision maker for this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient lacks decision-making capacity" -> "No living will or named surrogate" -> "Identify closest family member" -> "Mother is closest relative" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Patient lacks decision-making capacity" -> "No living will or named surrogate" -> "Identify long-term partner" -> "Girlfriend of 12 years" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Patient lacks decision-making capacity" -> "No living will or named surrogate" -> "Identify adult child" -> "22-year-old daughter" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Patient lacks decision-making capacity" -> "No living will or named surrogate" -> "Identify sibling" -> "Older brother" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Patient lacks decision-making capacity" -> "No living will or named surrogate" -> "Identify sibling" -> "Younger sister" -> 60%
analysis: In the absence of a living will or designated durable power of attorney, surrogate decision-makers are typically determined by a hierarchy of familial relationships. Generally, adult children are prioritized over other relatives such as siblings or parents. Therefore, the patient's 22-year-old daughter would be the most appropriate person to act as a surrogate decision-maker.
